articles.title: What's behind Trump's Ukraine-Russia energy ceasefire claim?
articles.summary: The US president made the announcement in a social media post, which was an apparent surprise to Ukraine and Russia is yet to comment.
articles.body:

Moscow is yet to comment on the announcement and Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky told US media it was "news to me".

Trump also recently announced a US deal to import Russian diesel, in an attempt to bring the fuel price down ahead of the midterm elections.

articles.title: 'Tartaruga-gigante' é encontrada morta em praia do litoral de SP | G1
articles.standfirst: Animal foi encontrado no sábado (10), na Praia da Enseada, em Guarujá (SP). O corpo foi removido pelo Instituto Gremar, que fará a necropsia para identificação das causas da morte.
articles.summary: Animal foi encontrado no sábado (10), na Praia da Enseada, em Guarujá (SP). O corpo foi removido pelo Instituto Gremar, que fará a necropsia para identificação das causas da morte.
articles.body:
Uma tartaruga-de-couro ( Dermochelys coriacea ), com 1,65 metro de carapaça, foi encontrada morta na faixa de areia da Praia da Enseada, em Guarujá , no litoral de São Paulo . O animal, também conhecido como tartaruga-gigante, teve o corpo removido do local pelo Instituto Gremar.

A equipe do instituto foi acionada por volta das 11h30 de sábado (10) para atender à ocorrência. Segundo a instituição, o animal já estava sem vida quando os profissionais chegaram ao local. A tartaruga era uma fêmea e pesava aproximadamente 280 quilos.

O corpo foi recolhido e encaminhado ao Centro de Reabilitação e Despetrolização do instituto, onde passa por necropsia para levantar informações sobre a idade e a causa da morte. De acordo com o Gremar, esta é a primeira ocorrência de tartaruga-de-couro registrada pela instituição em 2026.

O g1 procurou a Prefeitura de Guarujá para obter mais informações sobre o caso, mas não havia recebido retorno até a última atualização desta reportagem.

''Tartaruga-gigante' foi encontrada morta na Praia da Enseada, em Guarujá (SP) — Foto: Reprodução

No último dia 1º de outubro, outra tartaruga-de-couro foi encontrada morta na faixa de areia de Ilha Comprida (SP) . Na ocasião, o biólogo marinho Eric Comin explicou ao g1 que a espécie é a maior tartaruga marinha do mundo e pode ultrapassar 2 metros de comprimento e atingir até 900 quilos.

De acordo com Comin, diferentemente de outras tartarugas marinhas, a tartaruga-de-couro não possui uma carapaça rígida formada por placas ósseas. Em vez disso, o corpo é revestido por uma camada de pele resistente, com textura semelhante ao couro, característica que dá nome à espécie.

O biólogo também destacou que o animal realiza uma das maiores migrações do reino animal, cruzando oceanos entre áreas de alimentação e reprodução. A espécie está classificada como vulnerável à extinção pela União Internacional para a Conservação da Natureza (IUCN).

articles.title: VÍDEO: segurança de mercado e cliente brigam após discussão em Sorocab | G1
articles.standfirst: Testemunhas gravaram briga no bairro Éden. Confusão começou após cliente consumir produtos antes de pagar; rede de supermercado repudiou agressão e confirmou afastamento do agente.
articles.summary: O segurança de um supermercado e um cliente brigaram após uma discussão no bairro Éden, em Sorocaba (SP), neste sábado (10). Pessoas que estavam no local registraram a confusão.
articles.body:
Um cliente e um segurança terceirizado de um supermercado se envolveram em uma briga no bairro Éden, em Sorocaba (SP), neste sábado (10). Testemunhas que faziam compras no local gravaram a confusão com celulares. Assista acima.

Segundo apuração da TV TEM , o desentendimento começou após o cliente consumir produtos do estabelecimento antes de passar pelo caixa para efetuar o pagamento.

Nas imagens, é possível ver o segurança e o cliente discutindo. Em seguida, o homem é empurrado em direção a algumas mercadorias e imobilizado pelo segurança.

Briga entre segurança e cliente começou quando o cliente consumiu produtos do estabelecimento antes de realizar o pagamento, em Sorocaba (SP) — Foto: Arquivo pessoal

Em nota, o Mercado Chimar afirmou que "o cliente em questão já havia se comportado assim outras vezes e, sempre que advertido pela equipe de segurança, se mostrava indiferente às placas de sinalização que proíbem o consumo interno, bem como à abordagem da equipe de segurança, respondendo de forma desrespeitosa e desmerecendo o profissional que o orientava".

A empresa declarou ainda que repudia qualquer tipo de violência e não orienta que os colaboradores ajam dessa forma.

"No caso em questão, informamos que o colaborador envolvido não faz parte do nosso quadro, mas de uma empresa terceirizada que presta serviço de segurança para a rede Chimar. A empresa já foi acionada e informou que o colaborador foi afastado imediatamente após o ocorrido", diz o posicionamento.

articles.title: Boi Garantido: novas Cunhã-Poranga e Rainha estreiam em Parintins | G1
articles.standfirst: Evento reuniu torcedores na Ilha Tupinambarana para a apresentação das novas Cunhã-Poranga e Rainha do Folclore do boi-bumbá.
articles.summary: O Boi Garantido apresentou Lívia Christina e Isabelle Alcântara como as novas Cunhã-Poranga e Rainha do Folclore durante festa na Cidade Garantido, em Parintins.
articles.body:
Cunhã-Poranga e Rainha do folclore, itens do Boi Garantido — Foto: Divulgação

A Cidade Garantido, em Parintins , recebeu a nação vermelha e branca para o primeiro evento da temporada voltado aos torcedores. A programação marcou o reencontro do público com a agremiação e a estreia oficial de dois novos itens no palco: Lívia Christina, como Cunhã-Poranga, e Isabelle Alcântara, como Rainha do Folclore.

Segundo o presidente do Garantido, Marialvo Brandão, o evento reforça o compromisso da diretoria com os torcedores e marca o início dos preparativos para o festival deste ano.

A estreia das novas integrantes dos itens oficiais foi o destaque da noite. Lívia Christina se apresentou como Cunhã-Poranga, enquanto Isabelle Alcântara fez sua primeira apresentação oficial como Rainha do Folclore.

O evento também contou com a participação de outros itens oficiais do Garantido: a Porta-Estandarte Jeveny Mendonça, a Sinhazinha da Fazenda, Raíra Lins, e o Pajé Adriano Paketa. A Batucada Encarnada acompanhou as apresentações.

A festa também reuniu visitantes de outros estados. Um grupo de médicos do Rio de Janeiro, que está no Amazonas em uma missão de saúde, acompanhou as apresentações.

Segundo um dos profissionais, a experiência permitiu conhecer de perto a cultura de Parintins e a mobilização da torcida do Garantido.

Você pisca e aquela criança que até outro dia queria colo, contava tudo o que acontecia na escola e fazia questão de ter você por perto começa a fechar a porta do quarto .

Se você convive de perto com adolescentes, talvez conheça bem essa sensação: a de querer ajudar, proteger, estar presente… mas nem sempre saber como chegar perto.

É para tentar entender melhor essa fase tão intensa da vida que o Fantástico estreou a nova série: ‘Essa Tal de Adolescência’.

articles.title: Aeroportos da Arábia Saudita voltam a ser bombardeados | G1
articles.standfirst: Aeroportos de Riade e Damman foram alvejados neste domingo (11), segundo autoridades sauditas. No sábado (10), ataque ao aeroporto da capital do país deixou 13 mortos.
articles.summary: Novos ataques atingiram neste domingo dois aeroportos da Arábia Saudita, em meio à escalada de tensões entre de forças sauditas e o grupo extremista Houthis
articles.body:
Novos ataques atingiram neste domingo (11) dois aeroportos da Arábia Saudita , em meio à escalada de tensões entre de forças sauditas e o grupo extremista Houthi, financiado pelo Irã e que se tornou um dos principais conflitos atuais no Oriente Médio.

➡️ Segundo a Autoridade de Aviação Civil saudita, uma pessoa morreu e outras 11 ficaram feridas. Os aeroportos de Riade, a capital saudita, e Dammam foram atingidos neste domingo, de acordo com autoridades locais. Os Houthis reivindicaram os bombardeios.

➡️ No sábado (10), o grupo extremista já havia lançado mísseis contra o aeroporto de Riade, um dos principais hubs do Golfo Pérsico, matando 13 pessoas.

No aeroporto internacional Rei Khalid, em Riade, um projétil não identificado atingiu o terminal 4, segundo o governo saudita.

Os Houthis reivindicaram a autoria do atentado deste domingo. O grupo também afirmou ter atacado o aeroporto de Dammam e instalações da Aramco ao longo deste domingo. A agência de aviação saudita confirmou o ataque, mas não havia informado sobre vítimas e danos até a última atualização desta reportagem.

Homem espera diante de estação de metrô perto do aeroporto internacional de Riade, na Arábia Saudita, após ataque dos Houthis, em 10 de outubro de 2026. — Foto: Associated Press

👉 Os conflitos entre forças sauditas e os Houthis vêm crescendo nas últimas semanas e se tornaram o atual grande ponto de tensão no Oriente Médio. Os Houthis agem em retaliação à coalizão liderada pela Arábia Saudita que luta ao lado de forças do governo no Iêmen , que travam uma guerra civil interna contra o grupo extremista.

Também neste domingo, a Al Masirah TV, emissora do Iêmen controlada pelos Houthis, acusou a Arábia Saudita de um ataque ao o aeroporto internacional de Sanaa, capital iemenita.

Mais cedo, o grupo extremista havia emitido um alerta de risco para novos ataques a aeroportos da Arábia Saudita e pediu que companhias aéreas, viajantes e funcionários se mantenham afastados.

"Reiteramos nosso alerta a todas as companhias aéreas, especialistas, funcionários, trabalhadores e viajantes contra o uso dos aeroportos e do espaço aéreo saudita, pois são vulneráveis ​​a ataques e se tornaram alvo de operações para nossas forças, com exceção dos aeroportos em Meca e Medina (cidades sagradas). Instamos a todos a levarem nossos avisos a sério, e a Arábia Saudita é responsável por quaisquer interceptações malsucedidas", diz o post.

O ministro das Relações Exteriores da Arábia Saudita conversou com o governo iraniano sobre a recente escalada do conflito regional e os esforços para reduzir as tensões, informou a agência estatal de notícias saudita.

Ambulância estacionada no Aeroporto Internacional Rei Khalid, em Riade, na Arábia Saudita, após várias pessoas ficarem feridas por explosão. — Foto: Social Media/REUTERS

O ataque de sábado ao aeroporto internacional Rei Khalid, em Riade, na Arábia Saudita, ocorreu sem que o sistema de alerta de ameaças da Arábia Saudita emitisse qualquer aviso.

A ofensiva foi a mais mortal desse tipo no país em mais de uma década .

Segundo o jornal americano "The New York Times", Mohammed al-Bukhaiti, uma das principais autoridades do grupo rebelde do Iêmen, afirmou que a ofensiva foi uma retaliação aos bombardeios realizados pela Arábia Saudita contra o território iemenita.

O ataque forçou o fechamento temporário do aeroporto mas o Ministério da Energia da Arábia Saudita afirmou que uma conferência internacional de energia, planejada há muito tempo, ainda está confirmada para este domingo em Riad.

O Congresso de Energia da WPC, com duração de cinco dias, está sendo realizado em um centro de convenções a cerca de 10 km do aeroporto . A TV estatal informou que mais de 70 ministros, 300 executivos de empresas e representantes de mais de 25 organizações internacionais de energia confirmaram presença.

O presidente dos Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, afirmou que seu governo avalia participar dos bombardeios sauditas contra os Houthis.

"Talvez. Vamos analisar. Acabamos de saber do ataque mais recente, então vamos tomar uma decisão. Agimos muito rapidamente", disse Trump a jornalistas na Casa Branca.

articles.summary: A fumaça em Manaus atinge níveis críticos de poluição neste domingo devido ao aumento de 271% nos incêndios florestais registrados na região amazônica.
articles.body:
A densa fumaça de queimadas continua afetando a qualidade do ar e a visibilidade em Manaus e na Região Metropolitana neste domingo (11).

Às 8h, a qualidade do ar era considerada péssima em todas as zonas de Manaus . No bairro do Coroado, na Zona Leste, a concentração de partículas poluentes no ar chegou a 227,8 µg/m³.

articles.title: Corpo de homem com Alzheimer é encontrado no Rio Doce, em MG | G1
articles.standfirst: Idoso de 61 anos foi localizado pelos bombeiros na tarde deste sábado (10), no distrito de Pedra Corrida.
articles.summary: Idoso de 61 anos foi localizado pelos bombeiros na tarde deste sábado (10), no distrito de Pedra Corrida.
articles.body:
Homem com Alzheimer desaparece e bombeiros fazem buscas em Periquito — Foto: Corpo de Bombeiros

O corpo de um homem de 61 anos que estava desaparecido desde quinta-feira (8) foi encontrado na tarde deste sábado (10), no Rio Doce, no distrito de Pedra Corrida, em Periquito , no Leste de Minas. A vítima tinha Alzheimer e estava debilitada.

O corpo foi localizado por uma equipe do Corpo de Bombeiros, que realizava buscas na região desde o desaparecimento do idoso.

As equipes foram mobilizadas após o desaparecimento e fizeram buscas nas margens e na superfície do rio. Na noite de quinta-feira, os militares utilizaram um drone equipado com câmera térmica para sobrevoar áreas previamente definidas.

Na sexta-feira (9), os trabalhos continuaram com o apoio de uma embarcação. O canil da corporação também foi acionado para auxiliar na localização do homem.

Durante as buscas, testemunhas relataram ter visto uma pessoa em uma possível situação de afogamento no rio. Na ocasião, porém, ainda não havia confirmação de que se tratava do idoso desaparecido.

Com a localização do corpo neste sábado, foi confirmado que a vítima era o homem procurado pelos bombeiros.

articles.title: Incêndios no Amazonas: Governo Federal inicia combate com aeronaves | G1
articles.standfirst: Frota mobilizada em Manaus atua após melhora no tempo; comitiva do governo federal aponta surgimento de focos criminosos em áreas preservadas da floresta.
articles.summary: Com aeronaves e brigadistas, o Governo Federal atua contra incêndios florestais no Amazonas após identificar focos criminosos em áreas preservadas da floresta.
articles.body:
As aeronaves mobilizadas pelo Governo Federal para reforçar o combate aos incêndios florestais e à densa fumaça que atinge o Amazonas iniciaram às operações na região neste domingo (11). O começo das missões aéreas ocorre logo após a chegada dos aviões e helicópteros a Manaus e a realização de sobrevoos de reconhecimento para mapear os pontos críticos no estado.

A decolagem das equipes estava prevista para acontecer no início do dia, mas dependia de condições meteorológicas favoráveis.

O reforço ocorre em meio ao agravamento das queimadas no estado e após uma divergência entre o governo federal e o Corpo de Bombeiros Militar do Amazonas (CBMAM) sobre a oferta de apoio para enfrentar o fogo.

Segundo o ministro do Meio Ambiente e Mudança do Clima (MMA), João Paulo Capobianco, o combate intensivo aos incêndios, com lançamento de água, começou assim que as condições de visibilidade e o teto de voo melhoraram.

"Elas já começaram. A nossa ideia era que elas começassem intensamente hoje, mas tivemos um problema de teto. Veja que nós estamos aguardando para fazer o sobrevoo desde cedo, só conseguimos voar agora quando melhorou o tempo. Então, a partir de agora, todas as equipes estão de prontidão, iniciam as operações e, sempre que o tempo permitir, que houver teto para os voos, nós faremos os voos necessários", declarou Capobianco.

Avião modelo Air Tractor chega a Manaus para auxiliar no combate à queimadas florestais. — Foto: Jucélio Paiva/Rede Amazônica

O aparato federal conta com uma frota de 11 aeronaves, incluindo aviões do modelo Air Tractor específicos para lançamento de água sobre o fogo e caças/cargueiros KC-390 da Força Aérea Brasileira (FAB).

A operação integrada também conta com 290 brigadistas do Instituto Brasileiro do Meio Ambiente e dos Recursos Naturais Renováveis (Ibama), do Instituto Chico Mendes de Conservação da Biodiversidade (ICMBio) e da Força Nacional.

De acordo com o ministro, as aeronaves e brigadistas devem permanecer na região até que os focos de incêndios sejam apagados.

Após realizar sobrevoos de avaliação com autoridades estaduais e federais — entre elas o ministro da Integração e do Desenvolvimento Regional, Waldez Góes —, a comitiva constatou um cenário preocupante: a existência de centenas de pontos de fogo situados estrategicamente no interior de áreas preservadas, o que indica ação humana proposital.

De acordo com o Ministério do Meio Ambiente, além do fogo que se alastra a partir da queima de pastagens para rebrota, a presença de focos isolados na mata fechada reforça a necessidade de atuação da segurança pública para punir os responsáveis.

Diante disso, o representante da pasta fez um apelo para que o Governo do Estado empenhe a Polícia Militar ao lado do Corpo de Bombeiros no combate e na identificação dos infratores.

"É fundamental que esses indivíduos que estão agindo criminosamente vejam que serão punidos. Ou seja, é necessário combater a impunidade que está reinando aqui na região", alertou.

Uma força-tarefa do governo de São Paulo embarcou neste domingo (11) para apoiar o combate aos incêndios florestais no Amazonas. A missão reúne 30 profissionais, sendo 25 bombeiros militares e cinco integrantes da Defesa Civil estadual.

A equipe paulista levará equipamentos e recursos para reforçar as operações realizadas na região. Entre os materiais enviados estão drones, equipamentos especializados e 11 mil litros de retardante.

Segundo o Corpo de Bombeiros, os profissionais atuarão em conjunto com as equipes locais. O trabalho será concentrado no combate direto às chamas, na contenção da propagação do fogo e na proteção de áreas ameaçadas.

Amazonas registra 1,3 mil focos de incêndio

O Amazonas registrou 1.380 focos de incêndio nos primeiros 10 dias de outubro, segundo dados do Censipam (Centro Gestor e Operacional do Sistema de Proteção da Amazônia). O número representa uma alta expressiva de 271% em comparação com o mesmo período do ano passado, agravando a crise de fumaça e os impactos na qualidade do ar em Manaus e em dezenas de municípios do interior.

De acordo com o Painel do Fogo, a maior parte dos registros ocorreu em áreas públicas e de conservação. Entre os primeiros 10 dias do mês, 246 ocorrências foram em assentamentos federais, 116 atingiram terras indígenas, 97 foram registradas em unidades de conservação e 174 focos tiveram relação direta com o desmatamento.

Prefeitura, Estado e Governo Federal reconhecem crise

A Prefeitura de Manaus decretou estado de atenção em 24 de setembro, e a classificação segue neste domingo. Segundo o executivo municipal, o estado de atenção é adotado quando uma ou mais ocorrências afetam a cidade e há previsão de um evento de alto impacto no curto prazo.

Além da classificação da Prefeitura, Manaus foi um dos 36 municípios do Amazonas que tiveram a situação de emergência por conta dos incêndios florestais reconhecida pelo Governo Federal. O reconhecimento foi feito pelo Ministério da Integração e do Desenvolvimento Regional (MIDR) no sábado (10), mesmo dia em que o estado de emergência foi decretado pelo estado.

O ministro da Integração e do Desenvolvimento Regional, Waldez Góes, reforçou que o reconhecimento da situação de emergência nos municípios amazonenses, oficializado no sábado (10), permite a atuação integrada das forças de resposta e o repasse de recursos.

"Uma coisa é enfrentar em todas as frentes e empregar toda a força que puder, Governo Federal junto com o Estado e municípios, para apagar o fogo. articles.summary: Dados da Fenabrave mostram que cidade registrou 3.392 veículos zero quilômetro em setembro.
articles.body:
Foto de arquivo do trânsito na Avenida Andrade Neves, em Campinas (SP) — Foto: Fernando Evans/g1

Campinas (SP) ampliou o ritmo de crescimento da frota em setembro. Segundo dados da Fenabrave (Federação Nacional da Distribuição de Veículos Automotores), foram 3.392 veículos zero quilômetro emplacados no mês , o equivalente a uma média de 113 novos veículos por dia .

O resultado supera o registrado em agosto, quando a cidade contabilizou 3.145 emplacamentos e média diária de 101 veículos . O levantamento considera automóveis, comerciais leves, caminhões, ônibus e motocicletas.

Os números em Campinas acompanham o bom desempenho registrado no cenário nacional. Segundo a Fenabrave, foi o melhor setembro da série histórica, com alta alta de 8,32% nos emplacamentos em relação ao mesmo período do ano anterior.

"O mercado continua demonstrando demanda por veículos novos, mesmo em um ambiente ainda complexo de crédito. Para automóveis e comerciais leves, por exemplo, a concorrência entre marcas e os programas especiais de fomentação do setor, como o Move Brasil e Carro Sustentável, que têm reduzido preços e melhorado taxas de financiamento, continuam tendo peso importante na decisão do consumidor", destacou Arcelio Junior, presidente da Fenabrave.

🚗 Os carros de passeio representam a maior parcela dos veículos zero quilômetro negociados em agosto em Campinas. Foram 1.938 unidades , o equivalente a 57,1% do total.

🏍️ Foram negociadas 912 motos novas no mês, o que representa 26,8% do volume total. O melhor desempenho foi registrado em março, quando Campinas ganhou 1.094 motos novas .

articles.title: De ingressos para o BTS a cidadania australiana: as histórias do Círio | G1
articles.standfirst: Romeiros percorrem 3,6 km com agradecimentos pela saúde, pela casa própria e por conquistas pessoais. Procissão termina às 12h15, após 4 horas e 44 minutos.
articles.summary: O Círio de Nazaré 2026 reuniu milhares de fiéis em Belém com relatos emocionantes de superação do câncer, conquistas da casa própria e promessas inusitadas.
articles.body:
Círio 2026: promessa por show do BTS, homem vestido de canguru, superação do câncer e casa própria marcam relatos de fé — Foto: g1 Pará

Depois de anos em que percorreu o Círio de joelhos para fazer pedidos, Fabrícia voltou às ruas de Belém neste domingo (11) com uma imagem de Nossa Senhora de Nazaré de um metro de altura, feita de miriti. Desta vez, segundo ela, a caminhada tinha um motivo: agradecer. Perto de outros romeiros, Kauan Moraes, de 21 anos, seguiu de joelhos com uma placa que resumia sua história: “Milagre vivo, câncer vencido”.

Relatos de saúde, perdas, recomeços e conquistas pessoais marcaram a 234ª edição do Círio de Nazaré. Ao longo dos 3,6 quilômetros entre a Catedral Metropolitana e a Basílica Santuário, os fiéis expressaram a devoção em objetos, homenagens e promessas.

Círio de Nazaré 2026: Fiéis enchem praça Santuário na chegada da berlinda com Imagem peregrina — Foto: Juliana Bessa/G1

A imagem peregrina foi colocada na berlinda às 7h31 e chegou em frente à Basílica às 12h15, encerrando a procissão após 4 horas e 44 minutos. Durante o percurso, a Guarda de Nazaré cortou a corda entre as estações 2 e 3. Até a publicação desta reportagem, o número consolidado de participantes não havia sido divulgado.

Fabrícia levou uma imagem de Nossa Senhora de Nazaré de 1 metro de altura, feita de miriti, para agradecer pelas graças alcançadas. Ela contou que percorreu o Círio de joelhos por cerca de cinco anos, com pedidos pela saúde, pelas cirurgias dos pais e por um irmão que desejava ter um filho.

Neste ano, decidiu levar a imagem que mantém em casa porque não tinha novos pedidos. Saiu da Catedral às 5h30 e, pelo caminho, outros fiéis se aproximaram para tocar na santa e tirar fotos.

“E toda vez que acontece isso, eu penso: ‘Mãe, atende essas pessoas igual a senhora me atendeu’. Porque foram muitos anos eu vindo de joelho pedindo para me salvar de várias dores. E hoje eu tô aqui, só agradecendo”, contou.

Círio de Nazaré: Praça Santuário repleta de fiéis — Foto: Reprodução / Tv Liberal

No caminho, os promesseiros levaram símbolos das graças que atribuem à intercessão da santa. Uma casa de miriti sobre um chapéu, uma barriga pintada e uma corda particular de 25 metros também estiveram entre as formas de expressar gratidão.

Aline Cardoso, de 41 anos, percorreu o Círio para agradecer por ter conseguido comprar ingressos para três dias de shows do BTS em São Paulo. Diante da grande procura pelas apresentações, ela fez uma promessa que também envolvia presentear outra fã.

“A promessa era conseguir o ingresso para o show do BTS. E assim, muita gente não conseguiu porque a procura foi muito grande. E eu consegui os três dias. Eu vou os três dias”, contou.

Aline levou um totem para cumprir o que havia prometido: entregar o objeto à primeira ARMY — nome dado aos fãs da banda — que a abordasse na Praça Santuário.

“A promessa era que, se eu conseguisse o ingresso, eu ia entregar o totem para a primeira ARMY que me abordar lá na Praça Santuário”, explicou.

Giorgio Venturieri, de 61 anos, acompanhou a procissão vestido de canguru para comemorar a conquista da cidadania australiana.

Natural de Belém, ele escolheu um dos animais mais conhecidos da Austrália para representar o motivo da celebração durante o Círio.

Claudete Oliveira, de 49 anos, transformou a conquista da casa própria em uma homenagem que carregou sobre a cabeça. — Foto: Nicksson Melo e Rebeca Costa/g1

Claudete Oliveira, de 49 anos, transformou a conquista da casa própria em uma homenagem que carregou sobre a cabeça. Ela fez um chapéu com uma pequena casa de miriti, material extraído da palmeira do buriti e usado no artesanato paraense.

“Foi a realização de um grande sonho. Me inscrevi no ‘Minha Casa, Minha Vida’ há 20 anos e fui contemplada. Vim aqui fazer meu agradecimento a Nossa Senhora de Nazaré”, afirmo

De joelhos e com uma placa com a frase “Milagre vivo, câncer vencido”, Kauan Moraes, de 21 anos, participou do Círio pelo segundo ano seguido. — Foto: Nicksson Melo e Rebeca Costa / g1

De joelhos e com uma placa com a frase “Milagre vivo, câncer vencido”, Kauan Moraes, de 21 anos, participou do Círio pelo segundo ano seguido. Em 2024, ele foi diagnosticado com um câncer na região do fígado.

Kauan contou que passou por uma internação em UTI e enfrentou um ano de quimioterapia. Durante o tratamento, fez a promessa que voltou a cumprir neste domingo.

“Eu iria entrar em tratamento paliativo e hemodiálise. Quando soube disso, me apeguei à Nossa Senhora de Nazaré e, no outro dia, não precisei fazer hemodiálise, meus rins voltaram a funcionar”, relatou.

“Comecei o tratamento de quimioterapia durante um ano, um ano muito dolorido, mas nunca perdi a fé em Nossa Senhora. Eu prometi que, se eu saísse daquele momento, eu iria cumprir a promessa mais dolorosa e espalhar meu testemunho”, afirmou.

Círio de Nazaré 2026 em Belém: Suzy Paixão pede pela saúde do filho que está esperando — Foto: Nicksson Melo/g1

Suzy Paixão, de 25 anos, e Iran Luz, de 36, participaram da procissão para agradecer pela gestação de Miguel, após a perda do primeiro filho. Grávida de sete meses, Suzy teve a barriga pintada com a imagem de Nossa Senhora de Nazaré antes de sair para o percurso com o companheiro.

“Estamos aqui para consagrá-lo à Nossa Senhora, uma homenagem também porque perdi meu primeiro filho”, explicou Suzy.

“Se amparar à Maria nos deu força para estar aqui hoje e ela nos deu o Miguel”, complementou Iran.

Fiel segura um pedaço da corda do Círio 2026 — Foto: Juliana Bessa/g1

Por volta das 9h15, a Guarda de Nazaré cortou a corda entre as estações 2 e 3, na avenida Presidente Vargas, para evitar tumulto entre os promesseiros após o desatrelamento.

A estação 2 passou a funcionar como a cabeça da corda, e as demais seguiram atreladas no percurso.

Um dos principais símbolos do Círio, a corda reúne fiéis que ajudam a puxar a berlinda e fazem do esforço uma forma de agradecer ou pedir a intercessão de Nossa Senhora de Nazaré.

Durante a procissão, equipes da Defesa Civil usaram pulverizadores para borrifar água nos fiéis e amenizar o calor em Belém.

Rafael Tavares, coordenador de posto da PGM, informou que ao menos 28 atendimentos a pessoas que passaram mal foram realizados durante a Trasladação, na noite de sábado (10). Para a procissão de domingo, ele manifestou preocupação com a temperatura.

“Hoje, infelizmente, a gente espera um número mais elevado nesses atendimentos, por conta do fator climático, temperatura mais elevada”, afirmou.

articles.title: Mega-Sena: Aposta de Rondônia fatura R$ 26 mil | G1
articles.standfirst: Sem ganhadores na sena, prêmio principal acumula e vai a R$ 150 milhões; próximo sorteio acontece na quarta, 14.
articles.summary: A Mega-Sena premiou um apostador de Rolim de Moura na quina, enquanto o prêmio principal acumulou e pode pagar R$ 150 milhões no próximo sorteio de quarta-feira.
articles.body:
Uma aposta feita em Rolim de Moura acertou cinco das seis dezenas da Mega-Sena e faturou R$26.095,236. O sorteio do concurso 3.069 foi realizado na manhã deste domingo (11), em São Paulo.

🍀 Veja os números sorteados: 05 - 19 - 22 - 44 - 47 - 57.

Nenhuma aposta acertou as seis dezenas, e o prêmio principal acumulou. A estimativa para o próximo sorteio, que será realizado na quarta-feira (14), é de R$ 150 milhões, segundo a Caixa.

5 acertos: 150 apostas ganhadoras, que levaram R$ 26.095,23 cada;

4 acertos: 9.096 apostas ganhadoras, com R$ 709,33 para cada ganhador.

A aposta premiada em Rondônia foi um jogo simples de seis números, feita presencialmente em uma lotérica de Rolim de Moura.

As apostas podem ser realizadas até as 20h (horário de Brasília) em qualquer lotérica do país ou por meio do site e aplicativo Loterias Caixa, disponíveis em smartphones, computadores e outros dispositivos.

Já os bolões digitais poderão ser comprados até as 20h30, exclusivamente pelo portal Loterias Online e pelo aplicativo.

O pagamento da aposta online pode ser realizado via PIX, cartão de crédito ou pelo internet banking, para correntistas da Caixa. É preciso ter 18 anos ou mais para participar.

A probabilidade de vencer em cada concurso varia de acordo com o número de dezenas jogadas e do tipo de aposta realizada. Para um jogo simples, com apenas seis dezenas, que custa R$ 6, a probabilidade de ganhar o prêmio milionário é de 1 em 50.063.860, segundo a Caixa.

Já para uma aposta com 20 dezenas (limite máximo), com o preço de R$ 232.560,00, a probabilidade de acertar o prêmio é de 1 em 1.292, ainda de acordo com a instituição.

articles.title: A 26-acre California site was being turned into an ICE detention facility without a full environmental review; a federal judge has now halted construction until the government completes the required analysis
articles.summary: A federal judge has issued a preliminary injunction to stop the construction of an ICE detention facility in Gilroy, California, citing the need for a thorough environmental review. This ruling comes amidst concerns over hazardous materials and the facility's impact on local infrastructure and wildlife.
articles.body: A federal judge has halted construction of a planned Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) facility near Gilroy, California, ruling that the federal government must address environmental review requirements before the project can proceed.US District Judge Eumi Lee granted a preliminary injunction on Friday, September 11, in a lawsuit brought by California Attorney General Rob Bonta and Santa Clara County. The order keeps construction on hold while the court considers the next steps in the case.The dispute centres on a 24.5-acre property in an unincorporated area of Santa Clara County that the federal government leased in January 2025 for use as a potential ICE holding facility. State and county officials argued that construction began without the required environmental assessment or consultation with local authorities.Judge cites environmental risks at proposed ICE siteIn her ruling, Lee found that the county and state had identified specific environmental harms that could result from the development. The federal government, meanwhile, had not demonstrated that delaying construction would significantly obstruct immigration enforcement or cause substantial economic hardship.The site has raised concerns over possible hazardous materials left behind by a previous tenant, a pesticides research company, as well as the effects of construction on local wildlife, agricultural land and existing infrastructure.Another concern is the property's sewage capacity. The existing septic system was designed to accommodate about 40 daytime employees, whereas the planned facility could accommodate considerably more people on site.According to court filings, the federal government said the holding facility would accommodate up to 10 people, although its attorneys did not commit to a maximum occupancy figure. The ICE office would employ about 50 immigration agents, with approximately 60 people potentially visiting for daily check-ins.Judge Lee found that the projected increase in activity raised concerns about the septic system's capacity. In her ruling, she wrote that “either overburdening the existing septic system or constructing a new system pose a risk of irreparable environmental harm.”The property owner, Elmwood Capital Group, argued that it could make changes to the septic system to meet regulatory requirements. However, Lee noted that construction had already begun without the necessary permit process.Federal lawyers had described the work as an office relocation from Morgan Hill and argued that it did not require an environmental review. Lee rejected that position, describing the argument as “absurd and contradicted by the record”, according to the San Francisco Chronicle.California officials challenge federal processBonta and Santa Clara County filed their lawsuit in June 2026, seeking to stop the project over alleged violations of federal and state laws. Their legal challenge cited the National Environmental Policy Act, the Immigration and Nationality Act, the Intergovernmental Cooperation Act, the Administrative Procedure Act and California's Williamson Act.The plaintiffs argued that proceeding without the required review threatened land that has been protected for agricultural use since the 1960s. They also raised concerns about hazardous materials and the potential effects on surrounding communities and the local ecosystem.The federal government had previously agreed to pause construction until September 9. The Friday injunction continues the halt, with the court finding that the state and county were likely to succeed in their legal challenge.Bonta said the administration had attempted to advance the project without complying with environmental safeguards or consulting affected communities.Santa Clara County Counsel Tony LoPresti said the ruling reinforced the need to follow the legal process before developing a facility of this scale. He also questioned whether the project could be completed given the site's infrastructure limitations and environmental concerns.Parties must agree on scope of injunctionThe court has directed the parties to meet and confer before submitting a proposed order by September 30. Setting out the scope of the injunction.That process will determine what activities, if any, can continue at the property while construction remains suspended. LoPresti said possible work could include soil testing, inspections or installing fencing to secure the site.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Abhishek Banerjee faces fresh questioning in billboard row as police visit home again
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Police visited Trinamool Congress (TMC) national general secretary Abhishek Banerjee's residence in Kolkata on Sunday.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Police visited Trinamool Congress (TMC) national general secretary Abhishek Banerjee's residence in Kolkata on Sunday. They served a notice summoning him for another round of questioning in connection with the Camac Street party office billboard case, an officer said. This was the police's second visit to his Kalighat residence in a week to serve the notice.A team from Shakespeare Sarani police station reached the Diamond Harbour MP's residence to deliver the notice. The move followed a complaint lodged by the Kolkata Municipal Corporation (KMC). The civic body alleged that police personnel and civic workers were harassed and assaulted while trying to remove TMC signage from a building on Camac Street that houses a party office.Police had visited Banerjee's residence on October 7 for the same purpose. However, he was not at home at the time. No one was available to receive the notice, the officer said.On Sunday, the situation was initially similar. No one was ready to accept the notice when the police team arrived. After some time, however, the notice was handed over to Banerjee's staff at the residence, the officer said.The case relates to a disturbance on August 27. Police and KMC officials had attempted to remove a billboard bearing the TMC name and its twin-flower symbol from the building housing Banerjee's office on Camac Street in central Kolkata. The action triggered protests by Banerjee's supporters, who opposed the removal of the signage.Three FIRs were registered at Shakespeare Sarani police station in connection with the incident. Banerjee has already been questioned in one of the cases. He appeared at the police station and spoke to investigators for several hours. Police now want to question him again in the same case.The fire department had also separately served a notice in connection with the matter.Meanwhile, TMC spokesperson and MLA Kunal Ghosh criticised the police action. He objected to the timing of the notice, with Durga Puja just days away. Condemning the move, Ghosh said, "The BJP (government) has stooped so low that a notice has been served even after Mahalaya when the Durga Puja is just days away."Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: An 83-year-old Oregon blimp hangar was sold for $1 after a storm tore a 200-foot hole in its roof; after nearly 10 months shut, the air museum inside is now set to reopen on October 29
articles.summary: An 83-year-old aircraft hangar in Oregon, United States, which was sold for just $1 after suffering extensive storm damage, is preparing to welcome
articles.body: An 83-year-old aircraft hangar in Oregon, United States, which was sold for just $1 after suffering extensive storm damage, is preparing to welcome visitors again. The historic structure, known as Hangar B, houses the Tillamook Air Museum, which has remained closed since December 2025. The museum is now scheduled to reopen on October 29, following its acquisition by a nonprofit organisation.The building was badly damaged when a winter windstorm tore a hole about 200 feet long in its roof. The damage left parts of the wooden structure exposed to rain and other weather conditions. With the building requiring major repairs, the future of the museum remained uncertain for several months, according to The Oregonian/OregonLive.Things changed in August 2026 when Sean O'Brien, president of the Utah-based nonprofit Vintage Aviation Museum, agreed to purchase the hangar for just $1 and take responsibility for its restoration. He also bought the remaining assets of the Tillamook Air Museum for $20.The sale has since been completed, allowing preparations for the museum's reopening to move forward. Although the damaged roof has not yet been fully repaired, the new owners are working to restore the exhibits and prepare the building for visitors. The reopening will come after nearly 10 months of closure.Why was the historic hangar sold for just $1?The decision to sell Hangar B came after the December 2025 storm caused serious damage to its roof. The 200-foot opening exposed the interior of the enormous wooden building to the weather, making repairs an immediate concern.Initial estimates presented to Port of Tillamook Bay officials suggested that repairing the roof could cost between $2.5 million and $6.5 million. However, O'Brien believes the work can be completed for no more than $450,000.O'Brien, who grew up in Oregon and previously lived in Tillamook, had also volunteered at the air museum. His connection with the area, along with his experience as a general contractor, encouraged him to take responsibility for the building.Repair work will begin once the damaged metal section of the roof is removed. The Port of Tillamook Bay has hired a Seattle-based company to carry out that task. O'Brien expects the roof repairs to be completed by the end of 2026 or early January 2027."We are honored to reopen the Tillamook Air Museum and preserve its extraordinary aviation history for future generations," O'Brien said in a statement, "while working to bring this historic landmark back to life for the community and visitors from around the world."Built during World War II, survived for 83 yearsHangar B was built in 1943 by the US Navy during World War II. It was one of two enormous wooden hangars constructed in Tillamook to accommodate K-class airships, which were used to patrol the West Coast during the war.Both structures were built almost entirely using Douglas fir timber harvested in Oregon. Their size made them notable examples of wartime construction.Hangar B stands approximately 175 feet tall, stretches 1,072 feet in length and measures nearly 300 feet across. Its interior is large enough to accommodate six football fields.The original site had two such buildings, Hangar A and Hangar B. However, Hangar A was destroyed by fire in 1992, leaving Hangar B as the surviving structure.The Tillamook Air Museum opened inside Hangar B in the early 1990s, several decades after the building was constructed. Since then, the historic hangar has served as a space for displaying aircraft and preserving aviation history.What will change when the museum reopens?The new owners have said that reopening the museum is only the first stage of a longer restoration project. Their immediate priority is to bring back the aircraft, exhibits and collections that visitors could see before the December storm.In an announcement published by Tillamook County Pioneer on October 9, the museum said preparations were progressing to welcome visitors again. It also confirmed that work was continuing on plans to patch the damaged roof.Beyond the initial reopening, O'Brien intends to restore other parts of the building and improve the museum. Plans include adding more aircraft, introducing new exhibits and interactive displays, installing flight simulators and organising additional events."Our goal is to not only preserve this remarkable piece of aviation history but also enhance the overall visitor experience," O'Brien said, "giving visitors new reasons to return time and time again."The Tillamook Air Museum will officially reopen on Thursday, October 29, 2026, at 10 am. For the reopening celebration, it will remain open until 7 pm.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Sunday urged students in Chennai to develop innovative solutions to global challenges and carry Tamil culture
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Sunday urged students in Chennai to develop innovative solutions to global challenges and carry Tamil culture wherever they go. Addressing the golden jubilee celebrations of Jaigopal Garodia Hindu Vidyalaya Matriculation Higher Secondary School, he said the ideas of young Indians would shape the future of both the country and the world."The new ideas and solutions needed for a developed India will not only shape the future of India but also of the world. Today the world is looking for solutions, and you have the potential to provide these solutions. There is infinite opportunity in India today. I want every youth to see his future on the same big canvas because this is your time. This is your opportunity. I have full faith that this dream of ours will be fulfilled. Together we will do it," PM Modi said.The Prime Minister urged students to dream big, expand their horizons and pursue their ideas fearlessly. He expressed confidence that their efforts would help India achieve its goal of becoming a developed nation by 2047.PM Modi invokes Tamil culture and heritageThe Prime Minister highlighted Tamil Nadu's cultural and spiritual heritage during his address. Referring to the first day of Navratri, he described his visit to the state and his interaction with students as a positive beginning to the auspicious occasion."Today marks the first day of Navratri—a sacred land of Shiva and Shakti. The privilege of visiting Tamil Nadu and the opportunity to meet the devotees of Goddess Saraswati make for a wonderful beginning to Navratri for me. I also witnessed the enthusiasm of my young friends; I can truly feel this positive energy and excitement," PM Modi added.He also praised the ancient Tamil classic Tirukkural, describing it as a valuable guide for those committed to learning throughout their lives. He recalled gifting the work to Russian President Vladimir Putin.Referring to his association with Kashi, his parliamentary constituency, PM Modi invoked Tamil poet Subramania Bharati's message of fearlessness. He encouraged students to act boldly, turn their ideas into action and remain open to new knowledge.From global economic power to hosting the OlympicsPM Modi outlined India's ambitions, including becoming one of the world's three largest economies, emerging as a global manufacturing hub and sending an Indian to the Moon. He expressed confidence that collective efforts would help the country realise these goals.The Prime Minister also referred to India's sporting ambitions. He said the country was working towards hosting the 2030 Commonwealth Games and pursuing its ambition to stage the 2036 Olympic Games.Growth in higher educationThe Prime Minister highlighted the expansion of higher education since 2014. He said the number of universities had increased from 750 to more than 1,300, while colleges had grown from 38,000 to over 52,000.He encouraged students to remain curious and continue learning, stressing the importance of education, innovation and new ideas in building a developed India.‘Make in India’, ‘vocal for local’ benefiting Tamil NaduEarlier in the day, PM Modi said India's overall progress depended on the development of its states. He reaffirmed the Centre's focus on strengthening manufacturing, infrastructure and job creation, highlighting the role of Tamil Nadu in the country's industrial growth."We need to strengthen the states to strengthen the nation, and therefore, the central government is promoting manufacturing in states like Tamil Nadu. The campaigns of the central government, be it 'Make in India' or 'Vocal for Local', are benefiting Tamil Nadu as well," he said.The event marked 50 years of Jaigopal Garodia Hindu Vidyalaya Matriculation Higher Secondary School and its contribution to education in Tamil Nadu.Get the latest India News and Live updates. He said he did not know whether the claims were true and would not comment on matters he could not confirm.AllegationsSince late September, The Wall Street Journal has reported several allegations of questionable conduct by Guilfoyle.Its first report said she told reception guests that the US could undermine the Greek government, promoted a Greek construction and energy company’s business interests, and allowed its lobbyist into private diplomatic meetings.Citing text messages, the Journal later reported that Guilfoyle asked a Trump donor to pay a $100,000 credit card bill shortly before her confirmation hearing, promising access to administration officials in return.Separately, British tabloid The Daily Mail reported that Guilfoyle had alienated US embassy staff in Athens and pushed the boundaries of behaviour appropriate for Washington’s top representative in Greece.You use AI every day. articles.title: Hundreds of thousands of abandoned US mines were left behind after mining booms; bats, snakes and bobcats now use them as refuges
articles.summary: Across the United States, former gold, coal and other mines are becoming important refuges for bats and other wildlife.
articles.body: Across the United States, former gold, coal and other mines are becoming important refuges for bats and other wildlife. Their tunnels, shafts and crevices can provide shelter in areas where natural caves are limited. However, unstable structures and environmental hazards make these sites dangerous for people and potentially harmful to ecosystems.Bat Conservation International (BCI) works with state and federal agencies to protect these underground habitats while reducing the risks they pose. Keeping people out of dangerous mines while allowing wildlife to use them remains a key challenge. Special barriers called ‘bat gates’ address this problem by blocking human access while allowing bats to fly in and out freely. At the same time, a national inventory is being developed to map abandoned mine features, identify potential hazards and help authorities prioritise sites that need safety measures.How conservationists are protecting bats in abandoned US minesAccording to Bat Conservation International, its Abandoned Mine Lands (AML) programme works with state and federal agencies to protect people and wildlife at abandoned mining sites. The programme supports the safeguarding process, from identifying mines and conducting biological and cultural surveys to meet environmental requirements and building closures.Before entering a mine, the team first assesses whether it is safe to proceed. Specialists then search for bats and signs of their presence, such as guano and piles of insect wings left behind after feeding. They also record historical and archaeological evidence found at the site. These surveys help identify valuable underground habitats while preserving evidence of the mines’ past.The surveys help authorities reduce risks to people while protecting the underground habitats that bats and other wildlife rely on for shelter.Abandoned mines are providing shelter for bats and other wildlifeDark, enclosed spaces make former mines suitable habitats for a wide range of wildlife. Bats that usually roost in caves and cavities may rely on these underground sites in areas where natural caves are limited. Mines can offer additional roosting options and reduce competition for shelter.Their isolation can provide wildlife with shelter in places where human disturbance is less frequent. This is especially important during hibernation, when human activity can make it harder for bats to survive the winter. Bat Conservation International (BCI) has recorded many other animals using these sites, including foxes, bobcats, weasels, ringtails, coati, javelina, snakes, frogs, owls, swallows, and insects. Some mines also support distinct underground microbial communities.Which bat species live in abandoned mines across the United StatesSeveral cave-roosting bat species use abandoned mines, particularly in the western United States. BCI identifies Townsend’s big-eared bats, California leaf-nosed bats, pallid bats, big brown bats, and various Myotis species among those frequently found in mines.Nectar bats are also occasionally spotted, especially in the southwest. The distribution of abandoned mines reflects the country's mining history. Coal mines occur throughout the United States but are most common in the east.The west has a particularly high concentration of abandoned mines, with estimates ranging upwards of 500,000. Many date to the 1800s and early 1900s, although some mining activities are much older.Balancing public safety with wildlife conservationAbandoned mines can contain unstable rocks, poisonous gases, and dangerous drops. Open shafts and tunnels may also collapse, while some sites create environmental hazards such as acid mine drainage, which can contaminate soil and water.According to the US Geological Survey (USGS), its USMIN project is building a national inventory of abandoned hardrock mine features using information from federal, state and tribal agencies. The inventory aims to improve risk assessment, support land management decisions and help prioritise hazard mitigation and ecosystem restoration.At individual sites, bat gates provide one way to address safety concerns without removing wildlife habitat. Their horizontal bars allow bats to fly through while preventing people from entering. The approach helps authorities balance public safety with the protection of underground ecosystems.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Legoland Windsor evacuated over burst water main
articles.summary: Some customers were forced to leave the theme park halfway through their visit on Sunday.
articles.body:
The Legoland Windsor attraction has closed abruptly due to a burst water main.

Customers were told to leave rides and exit the resort at lunchtime on Sunday.

Thames Water said it had to shut off the damaged main near St Leonards Reservoir to prevent flooding, which affected supplies to the theme park.

It said some local residents had reportedly suffered flooded gardens and it apologised for the disruption.

Merlin Entertainments, the operator behind Legoland, said it is continuing to work with local partners and thanked guests for their "patience and understanding".

One Legoland visitor, who came with her children from Cornwall, said the sudden evacuation felt "surreal".

The woman, who asked not to be named, said: "We were queuing for a ride and had got right to the front when, all of a sudden, everything stopped moving.

"Then they came out and said, 'Right, come on, everybody off.'

"Over the announcement system, they said there had been some sort of Thames Water disruption in the local area and they didn't have any water.

"We'd booked a night in the hotel and stayed there last night, so we're absolutely gutted because we've just had to drive home.

"It's a good five-hour drive to come up for a nice day, only to come back after half a day."

Thames Water said supplies had been restored and repairs were under way. It said it would provide an update on Monday.

A spokesperson for Merlin Entertainments said the resort was closed while Thames Water worked to restore normal service.

"We apologise for the inconvenience and thank our guests for their patience and understanding," the group said.

The BBC understands the resort will reopen on Monday under normal operating hours.

articles.title: Russia strikes Ukrainian power plant after Trump claims energy ceasefire
articles.summary: Russia struck a power plant in eastern Ukraine, contradicting President Trump’s announcement earlier Sunday that both countries agreed to an “energy ceasefire.” A local official who spoke with ABC News said that a thermal power plant in the city of Kharkiv was hit twice and on fire. Ukrainian President Voldoymyr Zelensky confirmed the attack, along with…
articles.body:
Russia struck a power plant in eastern Ukraine, contradicting President Trump’s announcement earlier Sunday that both countries agreed to an “energy ceasefire.”

A local official who spoke with ABC News said that a thermal power plant in the city of Kharkiv was hit twice and on fire. Ukrainian President Voldoymyr Zelensky confirmed the attack, along with multiple others.

“Unfortunately, Ukrainian skies have been infested with Russian ‘shaheds’ all day today. There have been glide bomb strikes and strikes on our energy infrastructure too. A power plant in Kharkiv was attacked this evening,” Zelenzesky wrote in a statement posted on the social platform X.

The strikes arrived hours after Trump claimed Ukraine and Russia reached an energy ceasefire deal .

“Effective immediately, there is an ENERGY CEASEFIRE in the War between Russia and Ukraine,” the president wrote Sunday on Truth Social. “Both parties have agreed. Do not break it!”

Zelensky was caught off-guard by the claim, telling Axios that the deal “was news for me. But if Russians agree to an energy ceasefire, Ukraine will agree.”

“Ukraine wants peace. The question is whether Russia does. The Armed Forces of Ukraine have received all the appropriate orders. We are awaiting clear details of the dialogue between America and Russia – and we expect Putin to follow through on what President Trump said,” Zelensky added in his statement on X.

Trump on Friday announced that Russia will supply oil for the U.S. and global markets, lifting sanctions on the Eastern European country and boosting its economy.

“I have just concluded a highly successful discussion with President Vladimir Putin, of Russia, wherein it was agreed that Russia will immediately supply over 300,000 Tons of Diesel Fuel to the American and Global Marketplace,” he wrote in a Truth Social post Friday.

The cost of diesel has skyrocketed in recent months. With the midterm elections less than a month away, the GOP is in tricky political territory, putting pressure on the Trump administration to address rising costs.

Democratic lawmakers have criticized the diesel agreement with Russia.

Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer (D-N.Y.) called it “filthy” and said the president was making a “deal with the devil.”

articles.title: In Springfield, Ohio, Trump must settle the MAGA vs Chamber of Commerce war
articles.summary: Springfield, Ohio, small business owners reveal what they need from Vivek Ramaswamy and John Husted on taxes, regulations, and immigration reform.
articles.body: At a rally in Ohio last week, President Donald Trump told his supporters that, "Even if you hate John Husted, even if you hate Vivek Ramaswamy, you have to go vote for them." It was a blunt assessment of the GOP’s respective candidates for Senate and governor, but one that Trump, who wins Ohio elections like Tom Brady won Super Bowls, knows is vitally important. Trump would laugh off the remark, saying that nobody really hates the GOP candidates. But he was making an essential point, especially in Ohio, which is the front line of the war between the traditional GOP and Trump’s MAGA base, much of it centered on the question of immigration. To hear from the Chamber of Commerce side, I spoke with Jim Lagos, who has lived his entire 75 years in Springfield, owns several buildings downtown, and has been a central figure in the attempts to revitalize the city’s downtown district. TRUMP TOUTS ‘GOLDEN AGE’ AT OHIO RALLY, URGES VOTERS TO DELIVER GOP MIDTERM WINS "You have to pull the trigger," Jim told me of efforts to bring the very pretty, but very empty downtown back to life. "My father always used to tell me 'Christopher Columbus took a risk.'" Jim, as is customary for civic leaders, had nice things to say about Democratic Senate candidate Sherrod Brown and gubernatorial candidate Amy Acton, both of whom he has met. But he is all in for Husted and even more so for Ramasamy, who he hopes will slash regulations to speed up the recovery of towns like Springfield. RAMASWAMY OUTLINES KEY CONTRASTS WITH DEM OPPONENT LESS THAN 100 DAYS OUT FROM KEY GUBERNATORIAL ELECTION "We have temporary cuts on taxes for small business in Ohio," Jim said. "But they need to be extended. Big companies got a permanent break, because they are smart enough to donate to both parties." Over the past three decades, Jim has rehabilitated several historic buildings in Springfield and succeeded in filling most of the space with occupants. "Sometimes, when business is struggling, you have to carry them for a while until it gets better," he said. ICE PREPARES MAJOR OPERATION TARGETING HAITIANS LOSING TPS AFTER SUPREME COURT RULING The issue that most bitterly divides the business leaders in Springfield from the MAGA base of Trump voters in the area is immigration, and in particular, the wave of 15,000 Haitian refugees who arrived between 2020 and 2025, overwhelming schools, housing stock, and even the Bureau of Motor Vehicles, according to locals. Jim admits that the messaging, including the idea that Haitian migrants are better workers who don’t do drugs and want overtime, not only missed the mark, but downright offended many local native residents. Ramaswamy has, in the past veered toward a similar sentiment, which Frank, who works construction in the area, took some issue with. "I don’t like his idea that immigrants are, like, making us better from competition, I’d rather put Americans first," Frank said. According to Walter Curt, an investigative journalist who lives in Springfield, "When Trump came to office the first time, a bunch of factories got built in the area, and as soon as Biden got in, he staffed them with Haitians, effectively," through tax breaks to temp companies and business owners. DEM SENATE CANDIDATE SHERROD BROWN CLAIMS HE SUPPORTS 'CLOSING THE BORDER'; GOP SAYS RECORD PROVES OTHERWISE Importantly, while Curt does hold current Ohio governor and well known loather of President Trump, Mike DeWine, culpable for the Haitian situation, he does not blame the Haitians themselves, or Husted or Ramaswamy. "The entire country of Haiti would be in his front yard [Ohio] if it was up to DeWine," Curt said. "If anybody believes Vivek is of the same mind, I haven’t seen any evidence of that." AMERICA NEEDS WORKERS, BUT TRUMP'S POLICIES ARE SHARPLY CUTTING LEGAL IMMIGRATION Further complicating the immigration issue in Springfield is the fact that there is a largely Hispanic immigrant population well integrated into and assimilated with the broader community, something one does not see with the Haitian refugees. Victoria and Ambrosio opened Food Fusion, a large eatery with great food, a year ago, and they employ a mix of native born Springfielders as well as immigrants from Mexico, a dynamic you also see with the clientele. SMALL BUSINESS OWNERS BUILT THE AMERICAN DREAM. DEMOCRATS WANT TO TAKE IT FROM YOU What these first-time restaurant owners want from government is more transparency about regulations. "You don’t know everything that comes with it," Victoria told me. "As far as taxes, you have to know this, you have have to know that, and not just the rules and regulations of liquor licenses. There’s really no help for small business owners." Trump is correct that the vast majority of Republican voters in Ohio don’t hate Husted or Ramaswamy. Many downright love them. But in a close midterm race, the GOP needs those who don’t. articles.title: A 1936 Miami Beach hotel shut after Hurricane Irma in 2017 and became tangled in a $95.6 million foreclosure judgment; nine years later, its new owner plans to reopen the 45-room Art Deco landmark next month
articles.summary: A historic Art Deco hotel on Miami Beach’s Ocean Drive is preparing to welcome guests again after remaining closed for nine years.
articles.body: A historic Art Deco hotel on Miami Beach’s Ocean Drive is preparing to welcome guests again after remaining closed for nine years. The Tides Hotel, built in 1936, is expected to reopen in November 2026 following a multimillion-dollar renovation by its new owner, Safe Harbor Capital Partners. The 45-room hotel was damaged by Hurricane Irma in September 2017 and never reopened. Its closure was followed by years of legal disputes over an unpaid mortgage, insurance money and foreclosure proceedings that culminated in a $95.6 million judgment against its former owners. As reported by American real estate media company The Real Deal, Safe Harbor has invested millions of dollars in renovating the property and is in discussions with hotel operators and chefs to develop its food and beverage programme. The reopening would bring back a long-shuttered property at 1220 Ocean Drive, one of Miami Beach’s best-known streets.Hurricane Irma shut the hotel in 2017The Tides was built in 1936 and became a prominent Art Deco property on Ocean Drive. The 13-storey hotel has 45 rooms, including larger suites and penthouses created during an earlier renovation. According to Bisnow, the Chetrit Group acquired the hotel in 2011. In 2014, the company took out a $45 million mortgage from Miami-based Ocean Bank, secured against the hotel and associated properties. Hurricane Irma struck Florida in September 2017 and caused extensive damage to the building. The hotel closed and remained shut while the dispute over its financing and repairs unfolded. The scale of the damage made the renovation a significant undertaking. As reported by Bisnow, the estimated hurricane damage stood at more than $9 million. The hotel had undergone major renovations before the storm. A $35 million renovation completed in 1997 converted it from a 115-room property into 45 larger rooms, according to The Real Deal. Another $7 million upgrade was completed in 2008, covering guest rooms, public spaces, the pool and the front terrace.How a $45 million mortgage became a $95.6 million judgmentThe dispute began with the loan taken out from Ocean Bank. The mortgage was due for repayment in December 2020, but the borrowers did not repay the outstanding balance.Ocean Bank transferred the loan to Safe Harbor in January 2021. Safe Harbor subsequently filed a foreclosure lawsuit against companies linked to the Chetrit Group. According to Bisnow, the lender alleged that nearly $2 million in insurance proceeds connected to the hurricane damage had been deposited without the bank’s required approval. $1.2 million was transferred to Joseph and Meyer Chetrit, principals associated with the former owners.The Chetrit side disputed aspects of the case. In an email quoted by Bisnow in March 2026, lawyer Dennis Richard said: “The appeal itself of the final judgment is proceeding with full force.” He added: “We believe the issues that our client will raise on appeal are well-grounded.” Richard also said that the insurance money, along with additional funds, had been used to repair hurricane damage and improve the property. Safe Harbor’s allegations and the former owners’ response formed part of the wider legal dispute.The case went through several stages. A lower-court ruling in 2022 was overturned on appeal in 2024, and the matter was reheard. Following a trial in November 2025, the court ruled in favour of Safe Harbor and entered a judgment totalling $95.6 million, including the outstanding debt, interest and other amounts. In March 2026, Safe Harbor acquired the hotel and associated properties at a foreclosure auction. As reported by Bisnow, the auction concluded after about a minute of bidding, with Safe Harbor acquiring the property for a $10,300 bid. The Chetrit Group continued to challenge the final judgment through an appeal, according to the reports.New owner plans a fresh startWith control of the property secured, Safe Harbor has moved ahead with plans to renovate the hotel and prepare it for reopening. According to The Real Deal, the company obtained a mortgage of about $44 million from Maxim Credit Group, with part of the financing intended to support upgrades. The financing covers the hotel and nearby properties, including sites on Collins Avenue and a parking garage.The hotel’s location on Ocean Drive gives it a place in Miami Beach’s Art Deco landscape, which attracts visitors for its architecture, restaurants and nightlife. The Tides has also drawn celebrity guests over the years. Its visitors have included Marilyn Monroe, Jennifer Lopez, Ben Affleck, Jamie Foxx and Paris Hilton. The planned reopening is scheduled for November 2026, according to reports. The hotel’s return will end a closure that began after Hurricane Irma, although the reopening date remains a plan rather than a confirmation that guests have already checked in.You use AI every day. articles.title: A coal millionaire donated 3,654 acres to Pennsylvania in 1969; the state spent $1.7 million reclaiming mining-scarred land to create Hillman State Park
articles.summary: In 1969, James F. Hillman, president of the Harmon Creek Coal Corporation, donated 3,654 acres to the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania for outdoor recreation.
articles.body: In 1969, James F. Hillman, president of the Harmon Creek Coal Corporation, donated 3,654 acres to the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania for outdoor recreation. According to the Pennsylvania Department of Conservation and Natural Resources (DCNR), the gift was reported at the time to be the largest single land donation for a state park in the country, valued at more than one million dollars. The land had been used for oil drilling and coal strip mining, and known abandoned mine drainage problems existed on the site. From 1970 through 1977, the state spent $1.7 million on reclamation projects at Hillman State Park.How did a coal millionaire’s 3,654 acres become a Pennsylvania state parkSettlement in the region was limited because of continued conflicts between settlers and Native Americans, and settlements were frequently attacked over land ownership disputes. Many settlers built forts made up of a central structure surrounded by a stockade. Matthew Dillow settled the land along Dilloe Run in the northern edge of the present park and, with other settlers, built Dillow's Fort in 1779. The fort was built along a Native American path that ran north and south through the area, as was Fort Dugan, located six miles north in what is now Raccoon Creek State Park. Matthew Dillow was killed during an attack on the fort in 1782, and the DCNR says peaceful occupation of the region did not come until the end of the 1700s, with much of the area given over to farming.Abundant mineral resources were discovered during the 1880s, and many farmers gave up agriculture for what the page calls a more prosperous opportunity. The Citizens Fuel Company drilled the first gas wells in the area. Oil was discovered near the centre of the park in 1885, and the boomtown of Five Points was born. According to the DCNR, a significant portion of the Florence-Five Points Oil Field lies under the park and was once one of the most prolific oil fields in southwestern Pennsylvania. The South Penn Oil Company drilled more than 170 oil wells in the park, most of which are now abandoned. The DCNR adds that there are currently 28 active wells owned by the Cassidy Oil Company of Florence.How did a coal company plant more than two million trees on mining-scarred landJohn A. Bell began strip mining for coal in a small area within the park in 1914, and that J.R. Elec operated a 17-acre deep mine along the southern edge of the park during the 1920s. The nearby Florence Mine was purchased in 1928 by the Harmon Creek Coal Corporation, which began buying the land that is now the state park in 1932. This was the largest bituminous coal strip mine in Pennsylvania, with more than 15 million tons of coal removed by 1968. The company built and maintained private roads to haul coal, and some of them can still be seen and are used to access the park. After the Second World War, augers were used for mining, and the former village of Five Points was eliminated during these operations.The company considered reclamation an integral part of coal mining and began conservation practices in 1937, well before the practice became law. The first statute passed in Harrisburg requiring only partial restoration came in 1945. The company's conservation department pioneered the restoration of strip-mined land, and restoration plans were made two years before an area was mined. Those plans included reusing stockpiled topsoil, contouring the land, adding fertiliser and planting a cover crop. According to the DCNR, the company ran a nursery that provided 30,000 pine, oak, ash, larch, chestnut and multiflora rose seedlings each year. By the late 1960s, more than two million trees had been planted in the southern end of the park, and grasses, clover and vetch had been planted in the northern and western sections. The company's wildlife programme included food plots of corn, sorghum and sunflowers, the stocking of pheasants for hunting, and the stocking of fish in the lakes and ponds.How did a coal millionaire’s 3,654-acre gift become a Pennsylvania state parkThe property became a state park in 1969, when James F. Hillman, president of the Harmon Creek Coal Corporation, donated 3,654 acres to the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania for outdoor recreational purposes. At the time, the donation was reported to be the largest single land gift for a state park in the country and was valued at more than one million dollars. As part of the planning process for the park, an Operation Scarlift Report was completed because of known abandoned mine drainage problems on the site. The DCNR explains that Operation Scarlift was part of the Land and Water Conservation and Reclamation Fund, authorised in 1967 for the elimination of land and water scars created by past coal mining practices.The Department of Environmental Resources, now the DCNR, spent $1.7 million from 1970 through 1977 to complete reclamation projects at Hillman State Park. The work covered filling, grading, erosion control, soil treatment with fly ash and additional plantings. The DCNR's account therefore links the park's creation to two separate efforts: the company's earlier conservation practices and the state-funded reclamation that followed the donation.1949 model aeroplane field become a Pennsylvania state park airportIn 1949, an engineering student from the University of Pittsburgh asked James F. Hillman for a place to fly model aeroplanes. Mr Hillman contributed a 20-acre fenced area at the southern end of the park, which had a two-section field, a 200-foot asphalt runway, an operations building and a public address system. It was called Hillman's Model Wing Airport. The airfield closed in 1977, and a new one was built at the northern end of the park. It was named after K. Leroy Irvis, an aviation and model aeroplane enthusiast and a former state representative and Speaker of the House, who helped obtain funding for the project. The DCNR says the K. Leroy Irvis Radio Control Model Airport is ADA accessible and includes a covered shelter, asphalt runways and taxiways, asphalt and grass pit areas, wind sock poles, a frequency board, a parking area and a spectator area.The airport is operated and maintained by the Greater Pittsburgh Aero Radio Control Society, a chartered club of the Academy of Model Aeronautics (AMA). All users must have an FCC license, maintain and display a current AMA membership, and preregister with Raccoon Creek State Park, which can be contacted at 724-899-2200. The park's history page also records the Lyle Covered Bridge, built in 1887. It is a 38-foot queen post truss bridge on Kramer Road that crosses Brush Run at the eastern border of the park. It is listed on the National Register of Historic Places, is owned by Washington County and is open to vehicles and pedestrians.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.
